lines: One week passed.
The sniper attack at that party drastically changed the city's situation.
With the beloved “close aide” murdered, Balalaika was enraged, and the planned “hand‑off” was completely overturned.
Under the pretext of “revenge,” the Hotel Moscow resumed its invasion,
and the local gangs, having lost the support of powerful backers after the failed assassination, had no strength to push back.
Eventually the conflict ended—
and Hotel Moscow, led by Balalaika, finally seized the majority of the city’s interests.
Me
…So, can I be even angrier about this? In a situation like this?
Balalaika
Heh, who knows? Do as you please.
Balalaika
But I’m also feeling guilty, so I’m honestly following your wishes, right?
Me
Well, yeah, that’s…
This is a private beach in the city’s resort district.
Balalaika, her goddess‑like beautiful body wrapped in a vivid swimsuit, lies relaxed with a serene expression,
and beside her I stand holding a bottle of sun‑oil.
On the day of the party a week ago— I was shot in the chest by an assassin, yet of course I survived.
Me
You knew, didn’t you, Balalaika? About my… strange ability.
Balalaika
Yes. A little from Asagi. And, of course, when I decided to make you my “attendant,” I did some digging on my end as well.
Balalaika
Your odd power. And how you’d act in a situation like that.
Me
That’s… well, I can’t compete at all.
I gave a wry smile at Balalaika’s words and shook my head.
The fact that I, shot through the chest, am still alive now,
is thanks to the “demon” power sleeping deep behind my unopened right eye.
Because of this power I possess an almost immortal regenerative ability, so a gunshot can’t be fatal.
Balalaika used that as the “spark” to reignite the conflict.
In other words, that sniper incident at the party was a self‑inflicted act by Hotel Moscow.
Balalaika made everyone think I was her cherished young aide by taking me around.
That became a shield against assassination, and her death served as an excuse to restart the conflict.
It was all part of the plan from the start.
The renewed war ended with Hotel Moscow’s victory, and as a literal “life‑on‑the‑line” contributor, I was given this as an apology and reward, spending time on the beach with Balalaika.
Balalaika
Well then, Kotaro, aren’t you going to rub some oil on me?
Balalaika
You were the one who suggested it—spending the day on the beach with me “like lovers.”
Me
Uh, that’s… that’s true, but…
I held a bottle of suntan oil and forced a wry smile.
Something completely unexpected was happening.
Me
No, I thought Balalaika would be more… helpful. This doesn’t feel like revenge, you know.
Balalaika
Oh? “Revenge”?
Balalaika, lying on the sheet, looked at me with a delighted grin.
Me
Yeah. Of course I’d want to get a little revenge.
Me
I get that deceiving the enemy means using your allies—
Me
—but I’ve taken my fair share of pain too.
Even a half‑immortal body feels pain when it hurts.
So I simply wanted to spend time with this terrifyingly beautiful woman, and as a twisted payback for being used as a “spark” in the conflict without my knowledge, I demanded this beach time.
The absurd request to be “like lovers” came bundled with it.
But this was unexpected.
Balalaika wasn’t refusing at all; she was actually enjoying the beach time.
Hehe, sorry I couldn’t meet your expectations. But there’s nothing troubling me at all.
Balalaika
It’s only natural to lavish hospitality on a hero who devoted himself to the plan. I have the capacity for that, too.
Balalaika
It's only natural to lavish hospitality on a hero who devoted himself to the plan. I have the capacity for that, too.
Me
Isn't it a waste of time to deal with a kid like me?
Balalaika
I don't think so. Besides, Kotaro—
Balalaika
I don't dislike young guys like you.
Me
When I asked back, Balalaika smiled gently and whispered.
Balalaika
You cling to a foolishly noble ideal and throw yourself into serving the nation or an organization—
Balalaika
I used to be that kind of person too. Before I lost everything and ended up like this,
Me
So... are you praising me?
Balalaika
Huh? Did you not hear it that way?
Balalaika
Anyway, if this level of play is all you want, I'm happy to keep you company— that's what I mean.
Me
Ah, thank you.
She laughed merrily as if she could see through my childish mischievous heart.
Everything was in the palm of her hand— I was reminded once again how outmatched I was.
Balalaika
More than that—you're the strange one here.
Me
Balalaika?
Suddenly Balalaika said that to me.
Balalaika
Even though you have a body close to immortality, I've heard you have drawbacks when you're injured.
Balalaika
And yet you don't seem to resent me for devising that operation.
Balalaika
Why? I was prepared to be verbally abused and cursed.
Me
Because I know that operation also carried risk for you.
Balalaika
Oh—
Balalaika narrowed her eyes with a look of enjoyment.
Me
The fired bullets are large-caliber rounds standard to the West, like those used by UCOA—
Me
They can easily pierce a human body without armor.
In other words, at that moment, depending on my actions, she could have been hit too.
If I hadn't shielded her and diverted the trajectory.
Balalaika
Well, the powerful people in this city are tough. If we don't put on a convincing 'act' to that extent, they'll see through our intentions.
To deceive the enemy, you need to start from your allies—.
It’s the same reason she didn’t inform me of the sniper.
Because we staged such a truly pressing crisis, she could get the spark to reignite the war.
Me
So that’s Balalaika’s way, huh?
Me
Treating everything, including my own life, equally as a pawn for achieving the goal.
I took the risk after weighing my abilities, personality, and the city’s situation, and secured victory.
Me
A will like steel, cold‑bloodedness. There are parts I can’t understand, but I really think it’s amazing.
Balalaika
You’re overestimating me, Kotaro. I’m just a war‑lover who can’t get enough of battle—
Balalaika
Just an irredeemably crazy villain. There’s nothing to be praised about.
Me
Even so, I truly respect you, Balalaika.
Balalaika
Oh dear—
She shrugs and laughs as if saying “no treatment needed.”
Balalaika
Honestly, it’s amusing. I can see why Asagi has an eye on you—
Balalaika
Now, could you hurry and apply some oil? The sun in this country is a bit harsh on my skin.
Me
Y‑yes…!
My oil‑slicked hand gently brushed the back of the calmly smiling Balalaika.
